claim: A compiled authored host observer enforces the same complete import-stub access intervals and reduces local native-parser observation overhead.
scope: Instrumentation checkpoint only; original game remains isolated in Unicorn. No full-match throughput, complete machine-state coverage, rollback, or Android equivalence is claimed.

implementation.public_adapter_difference: Same observer implementation with explicit observer_library argument and ordinary sibling import; no workspace-relative dependency discovery.

negative_paths: native and adapter reads/writes overlapping either stub interval
inner emulation violation surfaced to both callers with one retained event
Python/native range configuration drift rejected before execution
native register-read and stop API failures remain fatal
first nonzero stop failure retained across later callbacks
positive_paths: callback, library and user-data lifetime retained after caller garbage collection

benchmark.scope: 50 native parses of the same 5,082-byte asset; local microbenchmark, no full-match throughput claim.

limitations: Uses Unicorn 2.1.4 private Python backend ABI and an explicitly loaded locally built observer library; not a portable ABI guarantee.
Rejection does not imply rollback: native stores may have executed before emulation returns. Discard failed engines.
Nested execution at an invalid PC followed by attempted recovery crashed both the reference and compiled observers inside Unicorn. Failed nested engines must not be resumed.
The same reference host-wrapper limitation remains: a bound memory method captured before installation can bypass the wrapper. Current adapters use dynamic methods.
Mapped memory and 87 registers do not cover opaque emulator state, every register, all callback globals, or complete host runtime state.
This microbenchmark is not representative full-data or full-match throughput.
